Methods

SCCN develops an integrated, open-source methods ecosystem for EEG/MEG research — from data annotation and preprocessing to analysis, sharing, and large-scale compute. Each tool has its own site; the summaries below give a quick orientation and a link out.

EEGLAB

EEGLAB is an open-source MATLAB toolbox for processing continuous and event-related EEG, MEG, and other electrophysiological data. It combines an interactive graphical interface with an extensive scripting environment.

  • Independent component analysis (ICA) and artifact rejection
  • Time/frequency analysis and event-related dynamics
  • Source localization and connectivity
  • A large community plug-in ecosystem

Delorme A, Makeig S (2004), J. Neurosci. Methods 134:9–21.

Visit EEGLAB ↗

EEGPrep

EEGPrep is an automated, reproducible pipeline for standardized EEG preprocessing.

Summary and external link to be confirmed.

NEMAR

NEMAR (NeuroElectroMagnetic data Archive and tools Resource) is an open web gateway for uploading, validating, visualizing, and processing human electrophysiological data (EEG, MEG, iEEG) shared on OpenNeuro.

  • Browse and search openly shared EEG/MEG/iEEG datasets
  • Automated quality control and visualization
  • High-performance processing via the Neuroscience Gateway (NSG)
Visit NEMAR ↗

EEGDash

EEGDash provides programmatic access to EEG datasets for analysis and machine-learning workflows.

Summary and external link to be confirmed.

HED

Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED) is a system for annotating the events in neuroimaging, physiological, and behavioral data using a standardized, extensible vocabulary — making event information machine-actionable and comparable across datasets and studies.
